Supplies food grains under TPDS and welfare schemes.

blocks.content: The core functions of FCI revolve around effective price support for farmers, widespread distribution via PDS, and maintaining buffer stocks to safeguard national food security.

rows: Supply essential foodgrains to vulnerable populations
Fair Price Shops (FPS) via TPDS / NFSA

items: Pay close attention to the distinction between the Food Corporations Act enactment year (1964) and FCI's setup year (1965).
FCI purchases foodgrains at Minimum Support Price (MSP), but issues them to states at Central Issue Price (CIP).
Buffer stock maintenance targets are fixed on a quarterly basis (1st January, 1st April, 1st July, and 1st October).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: FCI was set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964 to implement the primary goals of the National Food Policy.
It undertakes effective price support operations at Minimum Support Price (MSP) to protect farmers from distress selling.
FCI manages the distribution of foodgrains across the country for the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) at Central Issue Prices.
It maintains operational and strategic buffer stocks to ensure food security during lean periods and natural calamities.
Through the Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS), FCI intervenes in the market to check foodgrain price inflation.
